result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_topological_sort_order()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Sort nodes in topological order (DAG only). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L19193-L19325){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_topological_sort_order() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Returns a linear ordering of nodes such that for every directed edge `u -> v`, node `u` appears before `v` in the ordering. This is only possible for directed acyclic graphs (DAGs). Uses Kahn's algorithm (BFS-based) which has `O(V + E)` time complexity. The algorithm processes nodes with zero in-degree first, then removes them and updates in-degrees of neighbors. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : node IDs in topological order. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is undirected or contains a cycle (not a DAG). ::: ## Common Use Cases {.doc-common-use-cases} - build systems and dependency resolution - task scheduling with prerequisites - package installation order - Makefile execution order - database migration ordering - course curriculum planning ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Kahn's algorithm (1962) drives the sort: it maintains an in-degree count for every node, seeds a queue with the zero-in-degree nodes (the ones nothing else depends on), repeatedly dequeues, and decrements the in-degrees of each dequeued node's successors. Cycle detection falls out for free: if the queue empties before every node has been visited, at least one node must sit inside a cycle, and the implementation raises `ValueError` rather than silently returning a truncated result. Time and space are both $O(V + E)$. The output ordering is not unique in general; any node whose entire ancestor set has already appeared is eligible next, and the arbitrary tie-break here is whichever one the underlying queue serves first. ## Examples {.doc-examples} A small build dependency graph sorts so that every file appears after the files it depends on: ::: {#4445ffa2 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="main.cpp") .add_node(label="utils.cpp") .add_node(label="utils.h") .add_node(label="config.h") .add_edge("main.cpp", "utils.h") # main depends on utils.h .add_edge("main.cpp", "config.h") # main depends on config.h .add_edge("utils.cpp", "utils.h") # utils.cpp depends on utils.h .add_edge("utils.h", "config.h") # utils.h depends on config.h ) order_ids = graph.get_topological_sort_order() # config.h and utils.h always precede the files that depend on them [graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in order_ids] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['main.cpp', 'utils.cpp', 'utils.h', 'config.h'] ``` ::: ::: The same idea applies to course prerequisites, where the ordering doubles as a valid semester-by-semester curriculum: ::: {#a84d5551 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="Intro CS") .add_node(label="Data Structures") .add_node(label="Algorithms") .add_node(label="Machine Learning") .add_edge("Intro CS", "Data Structures") .add_edge("Data Structures", "Algorithms") .add_edge("Algorithms", "Machine Learning") ) curriculum_ids = graph.get_topological_sort_order() # Returns courses in an order that always satisfies prerequisites [graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in curriculum_ids] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['Intro CS', 'Data Structures', 'Algorithms', 'Machine Learning'] ``` ::: ::: A circular dependency has no valid ordering, so a cyclic graph raises an error instead of silently returning a partial result: ::: {#f5559d93 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "A") # Creates a cycle ) error_message = None try: graph.get_topological_sort_order() except ValueError as e: # The graph is cyclic, so no valid ordering exists error_message = str(e) error_message ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 'Graph contains a cycle - not a DAG. Processed 0 of 3 nodes' ``` ::: ::: When a graph has multiple valid orderings, any one of them may be returned: ::: {#1f62614e .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "C") .add_edge("B", "C") ) # Both [A, B, C] and [B, A, C] are valid; C always comes last order = graph.get_topological_sort_order() [graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in order] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` ['B', 'A', 'C'] ``` ::: :::
